records.summary: 2027 Chestnut St is in the NC-2 zoning district where a restaurant use is principally permitted on the first story. The site has operated as Pacific Catch restaurant since 2003 with an active Type 41 ABC license (beer and wine). The parcel encompasses 2015-2027 Chestnut St, with multiple restaurant tenants over the years. The immediate block is heavily saturated: 16 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft and 16 registered food/drink businesses within 500 ft, signaling high density. Over the last 10 years only 4 dated use decisions were found within 1,000 ft (too few for a meaningful approval rate), though all 4 were approved.

This is not a change of use: active Type 41 ABC license shows the space is already operating as a restaurant (Pacific Catch)
Subject parcel is 0491/001, which includes addresses 2015-2027 Chestnut St; records show multiple restaurant approvals across this parcel since 1999
High alcohol license density: 16 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft (including 1 Type 48 bar, multiple Type 47 full-bar restaurants)
Chestnut Street Financial Services Restrict Special Use District applies (restricts certain financial services, does not affect restaurant use)

Formula retail: the concept profile indicates this is a chain with 11 other locations; formula retail restaurants are principally permitted in NC-2 but may trigger Section 303 notification requiremen…
Merging storefronts: the profile states the project merges storefronts within the existing restaurant space; prior approvals show the parcel has historically operated as connected restaurant spaces
Immediate neighbors approved for entertainment: 2001 Chestnut St (The Dorian) received Discretionary Review approval in 2020 for Place of Entertainment permit with conditions
Only 4 dated use decisions within 1,000 ft in the last 10 years, all approved; too few cases for a statistical approval rate

comparables.why_comparable: Same parcel (2015 Chestnut St, part of 2015-2027 Chestnut), same NC-2 zoning, restaurant continuation. This is a 2021 DPH health referral for the existing Pacific Catch restaurant use at the subject address, 0 meters away.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 14 days for continuation of the existing restaurant use at this exact location. Since this is not a change of use but an enlargement within the same parcel that already operates as Pacific Catch, the Planning Department treated it as a continuation requiring only agency sign-off, not a Commission hearing.

comparables.why_comparable: Restaurant at 3347 Fillmore St (14 meters away, same NC-2 zoning), approved 2021 for continued non-formula retail restaurant use. Shows the distinction Planning makes between formula and non-formula retail in NC-2.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 7 days. Planning explicitly noted this was a 'non-formula retail restaurant' permitted under Section 711. The fast approval contrasts with formula retail cases that require CUA hearings, underscoring that formula retail status is the deciding factor for whether an NC-2 restaurant goes to a hearing or gets staff sign-off.

comparables.why_comparable: Restaurant with full bar (ABC Type 47) at 3318 Fillmore St (74 meters, NC-3 zoning), approved 2021. While in NC-3 rather than NC-2, shows how Planning handles alcohol licenses in nearby Neighborhood Commercial districts without triggering CUA for the alcohol itself.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 12 days. ABC Type 47 (full bar) was approved as accessory to a restaurant use in the NC-3 district without a CUA. In NC-2 and NC-3 districts, alcohol service incidental to a bona fide eating place does not require conditional use authorization; only bars (non-restaurant) and certain entertainment uses trigger CUA.

comparables.why_comparable: Restaurant with accessory billiard parlor permit at 94 meters in NC-3 zoning, approved 2022. Shows Planning's treatment of accessory entertainment devices within restaurant uses as permitted without CUA.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 6 days. Entertainment Commission billiard parlor permit (pool table and mechanical bull) approved as accessory to existing non-formula retail restaurant in NC-3 without requiring conditional use. Demonstrates that accessory entertainment in a restaurant context is treated permissively in Neighborhood Commercial districts.

comparables.why_comparable: Restaurant with ABC Type 41 at 3340 Steiner St (95 meters, NC-2 zoning), approved 2021. Same zoning district and alcohol license type as the existing Pacific Catch operation.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 14 days. Type 41 beer-and-wine license approved in conjunction with a first-story restaurant in NC-2 under Section 711. Confirms that alcohol licenses accessory to restaurants in NC-2 are routinely approved at staff level without hearings, provided the business operates as a bona fide eating place.

comparables.why_comparable: Restaurant at 3318 Fillmore St (74 meters, NC-3 zoning), ABC Type 41 approval in 2020, showing rapid turnaround for alcohol referrals in the immediate neighborhood.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 5 days. Type 41 license approved as accessory to a restaurant use in NC-3 under Sections 712 and 102. The 5-day turnaround illustrates that ABC referrals for existing restaurant operations are among the fastest Planning approvals when the use is already permitted.

comparables.why_comparable: Restaurant at 2120 Greenwich St (176 meters, Union Street NCD zoning), approved 2022 for ABC Types 47 and 58 (full bar and caterer). Shows how Planning treats off-premises catering and alcohol as accessory uses to an existing non-formula restaurant.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 21 days. Type 47 full bar and Type 58 caterer permits approved as continuation of existing non-formula retail restaurant use, with the caterer permit treated as an accessory minor use for off-site food sales. Demonstrates Planning's flexibility with accessory uses when the primary restaurant use is established.

comparables.why_comparable: Limited restaurant at 2101 Lombard St (112 meters, NC-3 zoning), approved 2020. Shows how Planning treats limited-service restaurants (similar to the subject's limited cooking profile) in nearby Neighborhood Commercial districts.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 8 days. Limited restaurant use permitted in NC-3 as non-formula retail under Sections 102 and 712 without superseding any prior building permit conditions or Commission motions. Confirms that limited-service restaurants are treated as permitted uses in Neighborhood Commercial districts without additional scrutiny.

comparables.why_comparable: Limited restaurant at 2095 Chestnut St (93 meters, same NC-2 zoning), approved 2019. Another limited-service restaurant on the same street, showing consistent approval patterns for this use type.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 25 days for a limited restaurant in NC-2. The similar limited-cooking profile and NC-2 location make this a strong analog for the subject's approval pathway, assuming non-formula retail status. Planning treated it as a health department referral with straightforward staff-level approval.

comparables.why_comparable: Restaurant at 3347 Fillmore St (14 meters, same NC-2 zoning), ABC Type 41 approved in 2017. Same location as other referrals, showing repeat approvals for the same property over multiple years.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 3 days. Type 41 license permitted in conjunction with continued restaurant use in NC-2 under Sections 711.44 and 790.91, with the requirement to operate as a bona fide eating place. The 3-day turnaround is among the fastest on record for this corridor.

patterns.pattern: Restaurant use continuations and enlargements within the same parcel in NC-2 zoning are approved at staff level as agency referrals in 3–27 days without Commission hearings, provided the use remains principally permitted.

Formula retail establishments in NC-2 require a Conditional Use Authorization and Planning Commission hearing (90–180 days) under Section 303.1, even when the underlying restaurant use is principally permitted under Section 711. Non-formula restaurants are approved in 3–27 days at staff level.

Alcohol licenses (Type 41, Type 47) accessory to bona fide eating places in NC-2 and NC-3 are approved as agency referrals in 3–14 days without conditional use authorization; only bars (non-restaurant) need CUA.

Limited restaurants (limited cooking, no full kitchen) in NC-2 and NC-3 are approved as agency referrals in 8–25 days under the same principally-permitted framework as full-service restaurants, with no additional scrutiny.

Accessory uses to existing restaurants (entertainment devices, catering, off-premises sales) are approved as agency referrals in 6–21 days without conditional use when the primary restaurant use is established and non-formula retail.

ABC referrals for existing restaurant operations in NC-2 and NC-3 are among the fastest Planning approvals (3–14 days) when the restaurant use is already permitted and the license is accessory to a bona fide eating place.

approval_signals: Continuation or enlargement of an existing restaurant use within the same parcel (2015-2027 Chestnut has operated as Pacific Catch since 2003)
No change of use: space is already a restaurant with an active Type 41 ABC license and DPH health permit
Restaurant use is principally permitted in NC-2 zoning district under Planning Code Section 711
No alcohol service addition, no entertainment, no late hours (closes before midnight) – all factors that avoid CUA triggers
Limited cooking profile matches other limited restaurants in NC-2 approved at staff level in 8–25 days
Multiple agency referrals for restaurant continuations at this exact parcel and immediate neighbors approved in 3–27 days without hearings
denial_signals: Formula retail flag: concept profile indicates 11 other locations, which would trigger a mandatory Conditional Use Authorization hearing under Section 303.1 even though restaurant use is permitted

Merging storefronts may trigger Section 312 neighborhood notification if the building permit involves a change of occupancy or square footage threshold, adding 30+ days and creating an opportunity for Discretionary Review filings
High license density (16 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft) may draw scrutiny in a CUA hearing if formula retail status is confirmed, though it does not block approval by itself

risk.concept_summary: A formula-retail restaurant chain (11 other locations) enlarging its existing Pacific Catch restaurant at 2027 Chestnut St by merging storefronts within the same parcel, with limited cooking, no alcohol service, and tenant improvements including structural and bathroom work.

overall.next_step: Confirm in writing with San Francisco Planning whether this chain qualifies as formula retail under Section 178; if yes, file a Conditional Use Authorization application immediately and budget 120–180 days for the hearing; if no, proceed with the building permit application routing through Planning…

approvals.summary: Formula retail triggers a Conditional Use Authorization hearing under Section 303 even though restaurant use is principally permitted in NC-2 zoning; the concept profile states 11 other locations, which meets the formula retail definition, so a Planning Commission hearing is required.

findings.text: An active ABC Type 41 license (beer and wine, eating place) is on file at 2027 Chestnut St in the name of Pacific Catch, issued 2003-05-08.
Zoning district NC-2: a restaurant on the first story is principally permitted under Planning Code Section 711 as it stood on 2022-04-17.
Zoning district NC-2: formula retail is a conditional use under Planning Code Section 711 as it stood on 2022-04-17.
Agency referral MB1101474 filed 2011-08-10 approved Type 41 ABC license in conjunction with a small self-service restaurant use at 2015-2027 Chestnut St (the subject parcel) under Section 711.42.
Non-formula restaurants in NC-2 are approved as agency referrals in 3–27 days; formula retail restaurants require a CUA hearing taking 120–180 days, based on N=10 comparable cases within 1,000 feet.

approvals.summary: Health permit to operate is issued after plan check and inspection without a hearing; the existing Pacific Catch restaurant already holds a health permit, so this enlargement will require DPH plan review and a pre-opening inspection.

findings.text: Agency referral 2021-000512MIS filed 2021-01-13 at 2015 Chestnut St (same parcel) approved DPH referral for restaurant continuation in 14 days.
DPH health permit applications for restaurant continuations and enlargements in NC-2 were approved in 5–25 days in N=10 comparable cases, all as agency referrals without hearings.

approvals.summary: Building permit and change of use status is insufficient information because the records do not establish whether the space is for fewer than 50 people or the existing occupancy group; a change of occupancy triggers Planning referral and possible neighborhood notification under Section 312.

findings.text: The concept profile states the project involves tenant improvements and merging storefronts within the existing restaurant, with structural and bathroom work, but does not specify the occupant load or whether the occupancy group will change.
Building Code Section 303 classifies a restaurant as Assembly Group A-2, and a space for fewer than 50 people as Group B; the existing occupancy group is not shown in public records.
Agency referral MB1000828 filed 2010-08-05 at 2015-2022 Chestnut St (same parcel) noted that Section 312 neighborhood notification was completed for a change of use under BPA 2010.03047560.

If the building permit involves a change of occupancy or merging storefronts increases the square footage above a notification threshold, Section 312 neighborhood notification is required, which adds 30+ days and creates an opportunity for Discretionary Review filings.

expected_conditions.condition: Operate as a bona fide eating place with food service available during all hours alcohol is served (Planning Code Section 790.142).
expected_conditions.basis: Agency referral 2017-005937MIS at 2001 Chestnut St (0 meters, NC-2) and 2017-008077MIS at 3347 Fillmore St (14 meters, NC-2) both required the restaurant to operate as a bona fide eating place per Section 790.142 when approving Type 41 ABC licenses in conjunction with restaurant use.

expected_conditions.condition: Limit hours of operation to 6:00 a.m. to 2:00 a.m. (principally permitted hours in NC-2; hours after 2:00 a.m. would require conditional use).
expected_conditions.basis: Planning Code Section 711 as it stood on 2022-04-17 specifies that hours 6:00 a.m. to 2:00 a.m. are principally permitted in NC-2, and hours 2:00 a.m. to 6:00 a.m. require conditional use. The concept profile states the restaurant closes before midnight, which is within permitted hours.

expected_conditions.condition: If formula retail status is confirmed, comply with the findings required for formula retail conditional use under Section 303.1 and any conditions the Planning Commission imposes to mitigate impacts on neighborhood character.
expected_conditions.basis: Conditional Use Authorization case 2010.0695C at 46 meters (NC-2) approved a T-Mobile formula retail store after a Commission hearing. Formula retail CUAs typically include conditions on signage, storefront design, community benefits, and operating hours to preserve neighborhood character.

expected_conditions.condition: Complete DPH plan check approval before submitting the building permit for plan review, and schedule a pre-final inspection at 80% construction completion and a final inspection before the permit to operate is issued.
expected_conditions.basis: The permit catalog entry for sf.health_plan_check states that any new food facility or remodel affecting the kitchen needs DPH approval of plans, finishes, equipment and menu, with a pre-final inspection at ~80% complete and a final inspection booked at least two weeks ahead.

expected_conditions.condition: Install grease-capturing equipment per the FOG Control Ordinance and submit the Installation Verification Form to SFPUC before the building permit final sign-off.
expected_conditions.basis: The permit catalog entry for sf.fog_wastewater_permit states that every food service establishment that cooks must install grease-capturing equipment, and SFPUC inspectors assign a Discharger Category that dictates the device type. An undersized or missing interceptor is a common reason DBI withholds final sign-off.

filing_playbook.action: Pre-application meeting with San Francisco Planning to confirm formula retail status under Section 178 and obtain a written determination.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Present the chain's standardized features (menu, décor, color scheme, layout, uniforms, signage) across its 11 locations and ask whether this meets the formula retail definition. If Planning confirms formula retail status, request guidance on the CUA filing requirements, environmental review, and community outreach expectations. If Planning determines this is not formula retail, obtain that determination in writing and proceed to Step 3.

filing_playbook.action: If formula retail, file a Conditional Use Authorization application with San Francisco Planning under Section 303, including the building permit plans, a formula retail findings package, and proof of a pre-application community meeting.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Emphasize that this is an enlargement of an existing restaurant that has operated at this location since 2003, not a new use. Frame the project as enhancing an established neighborhood business by improving the facilities and bathrooms, and merging storefronts to create a more efficient layout. Address the formula retail findings under Section 303.1: the chain serves sustainably sourced seafood, employs local staff, and fits the neighborhood's dining character. Note that the use is principally permitted and the only issue is formula retail status. Request that the Commission approve the CUA with standard bona fide eating place conditions and no additional restrictions.

filing_playbook.action: File the building permit application with DBI for tenant improvements, structural work, and bathroom upgrades, routing through Planning as an agency referral.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that this is an enlargement of the existing Pacific Catch restaurant by merging storefronts within the same parcel (2015-2027 Chestnut St), with structural work, bathroom improvements, and no change to the restaurant use or alcohol service. Note that the space has operated as a restaurant since 2003 with an active Type 41 ABC license and health permit. If Planning has issued a written determination that this is not formula retail, attach it to the building permit application and request expedited routing as a continuation of use. If formula retail CUA is required, note that the building permit is contingent on CUA approval and coordinate the DBI and Planning timelines.

filing_playbook.action: Submit DPH plan check application for the remodeled kitchen, finishes, equipment, and menu at the same time as the building permit application.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that this is a remodel of the existing Pacific Catch restaurant kitchen to accommodate the enlarged space, with limited cooking (no full kitchen expansion). Provide two sets of scaled drawings, interior and exterior photos, and a menu describing food preparation. Note that the restaurant has held a health permit at 2027 Chestnut St since 2003 and this is a continuation of the same use and menu. Request that DPH coordinate plan check approval with the building permit timeline so that the pre-final inspection can be scheduled at 80% construction completion.

filing_playbook.action: Schedule the DPH pre-final inspection at 80% construction completion and the final inspection at least two weeks before the target opening date, after the building permit final is issued.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Confirm with the DPH plan reviewer that all equipment, finishes, and surfaces match the approved plans, and that a certified food safety manager is on staff (required within 60 days of opening). Walk the space against the DPH checklist one week before the inspection to ensure hand sinks, hot water, sealed surfaces, and the grease interceptor are installed and functional. After the final inspection passes, the DPH permit to operate will be issued and the restaurant can serve the public in the enlarged space.

timeline_cost.notes: Time to approval: 120–300 days for a Conditional Use Authorization (if formula retail is confirmed) plus building permit, DPH plan check, and health permit to operate. The CUA accounts for 90–180 days (pre-application meeting, environmental review, hearing scheduling, 30-day appeal period). Building permit review adds 14–60 days after CUA approval, and DPH plan check and final inspection add 21–60 days. If Planning determines this is not formula retail, the timeline drops to 50–120 days (building permit, DPH plan check, and final inspection only, routed as agency referrals). Government costs: CUA application fee $3,100–$6,000 (depending on construction valuation and fee waivers), building permit $800–$15,000 (percentage of construction cost), DPH plan check $828–$2,500 (flat fee for remodel), health permit to operate $470 (FY2026–27 fee). Total government cost range assumes CUA is required; if not, subtract the CUA fee.
